trust_decision.summary: Whether a customer-supplied ticket attachment may be written to the web-served public disk with its client-controlled extension and content is decided by completeUpload() in each ticket Livewire component, which calls $attachment->store('public/ticket-attachments') with no mime, extension, size or content check anywhere and returns a public URL to the uploader.

landing_point.why: It is the only code in the tree that writes a client-uploaded file to disk, and the summary 'Remote Code Execution via public file uploads' points straight at the upload branch of the ticket form; a second byte-identical copy sits at app/Livewire/Tickets/Show.php:27-38.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /tickets/create (routes/web.php:41) -> Livewire App\Livewire\Tickets\Create::completeUpload(), called from the shared editor JS on the create-ticket page
GET /tickets/{ticket} (routes/web.php:42) -> Livewire App\Livewire\Tickets\Show::completeUpload(), called from the same editor on the ticket reply page

the shared <x-easymde-editor /> widget mounted at themes/default/views/tickets/create.blade.php:39 and themes/default/views/tickets/show.blade.php:34 (client-side wiring: uploadImage:true, upload-image toolbar button, imageUploadFunction -> @this.upload('attachments') -> @this.completeUpload)
fix_sites.module_kind: theme_view (presentation wrapper in themes/, outside app/)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Themes are presentation-only and are copied per install by 'themes:make' (app/Console/Commands/MakeTheme.php:43-47), so the blade is the deployment's theme rather than the application: the dangerous write is in app/ and a server-side type/content check would make the editor's upload button harmless, so the theme needs no change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The ordinary ticket create and reply flows must keep working: validate subject/message/priority, rate-limit, persist the message, notify and redirect (create()), and persist a reply message (save()); the shared editor also syncs markdown into $message via @this.set('message', ...) at themes/default/views/components/easymde-editor.blade.php:71-73. An over-broad fix (dropping WithFileUploads/$attachments in a way that makes the component's wire:upload update throw, rejecting any component update that carries an attachments payload, or removing the editor component altogether) breaks plain ticket submission and replies.

O6_input_shapes: any file extension / MIME type - store() applies no allowlist and no content check, so a .php body is stored as written
several files at once - 'public array $attachments' holds a list and each element is stored independently

an arbitrary client filename used as the lookup key in completeUpload($filename), so the stored file carries a client-chosen name/extension (the published fix handles all three only by deleting the sink rather than by validating a shape)

O7_producer.where: config/livewire.php:66-77 (temporary_file_upload.rules => null, i.e. Livewire's default ['required','file','max:12288'] only)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an attachment/reply method on the dashboard tickets widget, using the same WithFileUploads + store('public/ticket-attachments') pair
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project already copy-pasted completeUpload verbatim between Create and Show, so a third copy on the widget that answers tickets inline is exactly the shape a maintainer would write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a staff-reply attachment field using Filament FileUpload onto the public disk alongside the existing MarkdownEditor
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: staff already answer tickets through a Filament MarkdownEditor; adding an attachment upload there is the obvious next maintainer step and would copy the same public-disk write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second ticket surface (e.g. a guest/pre-sales contact form view) mounting <x-easymde-editor /> with uploadImage left on
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the editor is a shared blade component, so every new ticket-like page reuses it and inherits both the upload button and the imageUploadFunction wiring.

O9_family: CWE-434 unrestricted file upload written to a web-served public disk (webshell / RCE)

O10_build.toolchain: composer (composer.json:11-45; Laravel 12, Livewire 3, Filament 3) plus npm/vite for theme assets (package.json, vite.js); phpunit 11 with phpunit.xml
services: Redis is the .env.example cache store (.env.example:29) but phpunit overrides CACHE_STORE=array
O10_build.project_tests: Only tests/Feature/Auth/LoginTest.php, tests/Feature/Auth/RegisterTest.php, tests/Feature/CartTest.php and tests/Unit/{ExampleTest,InvoiceNumberTest}.php exist; there are no ticket or upload tests at the pinned commit, and the fix diff adds none.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a mime/extension allowlist to the first completeUpload() you find (or set uploadImage:false in the editor blade) and stop, leaving the second component and the client-side wiring able to reach the public disk.

out_of_scope_notes: Admin-only file surfaces exist outside this advisory (settings logo upload app/Classes/Settings.php:57-64 via app/Classes/FilamentInput.php:233-255 with accept => ['image/*'], and product/category image uploads at app/Admin/Resources/ProductResource.php:77 and app/Admin/Resources/CategoryResource.php:57); noted once, not pursued.
The extension helper's TemporaryUploadedFile handling (app/Helpers/ExtensionHelper.php:264-267) is admin product-config code and never writes to the public disk; outside this advisory.
unverified: Repository size in MB (no shell available in this session), so tiny_repo/giant_repo could not be checked.

Exact runtime reachability of the stored file: .env.example:30 sets FILESYSTEM_DISK=local, so store('public/ticket-attachments') lands in storage/app/public/ticket-attachments/<random hash>.<ext> while Storage::url() on the local disk prefixes an extra 'public/' segment (config/filesystems.php:16,33-37; Create.php:35-36). With FILESYSTEM_DISK=public the returned URL matches and the file is served under /storage/public/...; the deployment setting is not in the tree.
The advisory text itself is not in the inputs, so whether it names both ticket pages, or only the create form, could not be checked.
Whether hidden tests derived from a 'delete the feature' fix would accept a validation-based fix (mime/extension allowlist) instead of removal; the fix diff adds no tests to copy that from.
